goal: Expose msfslogger's logbook (flights, trips, planned legs, ACARS comms, live status) to a remote Claude client via an MCP server mounted inside the existing Express app, with 14 read tools and 4 additive/reversible write tools, gated by a new MCP_TOKEN credential and route allow-list that is fully independent of INGEST_TOKEN.
frozen_decisions: Add remote claude as a requirement. Running on the same machine as the server is an unlikely use case as the server is meant to run headless in a homelab scenario. (rules out stdio transport entirely)
Transport is MCP Streamable HTTP, not stdio.
The MCP endpoint mounts inside the existing src/server.ts Express app, not a standalone process.

Auth is a new credential (working name MCP_TOKEN) and a new route allow-list (working name MCP_SCOPED_ROUTES), modeled on src/auth/ingestScope.ts, kept entirely separate from INGEST_TOKEN/INGEST_SCOPED_ROUTES — revoking one must never affect the other.
Auth mechanism is a static bearer token, not OAuth 2.1.
get_flight_stats and search_flights are the only two tools with no existing backing route; every other tool in the inventory maps to an existing route in docs/api.md.

Write tools are limited to: update_flight_notes (notes field only, never aircraft), create_trip, assign_flight_to_trip, import_simbrief_leg. Deletes, combine, PDF, all SayIntentions link/import/clearance/send, and all settings/credential writes are out of scope for v1.
No IP allow-listing in v1 — security model is TLS + bearer-token secrecy only, matching INGEST_TOKEN's posture. Revisit only if Designer finds this insufficient.
All implementation in this run is backend-only (src/**, tests/**) — no client/** work.
sequencing_rationale: Design must freeze the auth model, the two new routes, and the MCP tool/transport contract before any code is written: three implementers will build against it cold, and a mismatch discovered mid-implementation (e.g. a tool's schema disagreeing with the route it wraps) is expensive to unwind on a brand-new external contract. Phase 1 is that freeze, gated by its own reviewer before phase 2 starts.

T-003 (auth scope module) and T-004 (the two new routes) touch disjoint files and have no logical dependency on each other — neither route needs MCP awareness, and the scope module needs no aggregation logic — so they run in parallel after the design reviewer, saving wall-clock.

T-005 (MCP server + read-tool wiring) depends on both: two of the fourteen read tools (search_flights, get_flight_stats) call the routes T-004 builds, and every tool call must pass through the scope gate T-003 builds to reach requireAuth.

T-006 (write tools) is sequenced after T-005 rather than parallelized with it: it registers into the same McpServer instance T-005 creates, and it is the highest-risk seam in the run (the only mutation surface, and the one place a field-scoping bug — aircraft leaking through update_flight_notes — would violate a stated success criterion). It gets its own task and its own fresh look in review rather than being folded into T-005.

T-007 (integration tests) runs last because its value is proving the read and write tool sets work together against one real MCP client connection over Streamable HTTP — the tool inventory count, one full read round trip, one full write round trip with field-scoping enforcement, and the auth-rejection path. That is the most direct evidence for success criterion 1 and is only meaningful once both tool sets exist.

Ship/DevOps is deliberately not scheduled in this plan: intake.md already defers that call until design.md exists and the actual env-var/deployment footprint is concrete. The Orchestrator decides after phase 1's review whether a devops task is warranted (e.g. documenting MCP_TOKEN alongside INGEST_TOKEN, or a reverse-proxy note) — inventing that task now would be guessing at scope the intake explicitly left open.

Read tools (14) and write tools (4) were kept in one file each rather than one file per tool: every tool in a group shares the same registration entry point and the same risk profile, so splitting further would buy diagrams, not parallelism (per the 'two edits to the same file are one task' rule, since all 14 read tools land in src/mcp/tools/read.ts regardless of how many are listed).

phases.name: Design freeze: auth scope, new routes, MCP tool contract
phases.ships: No user-visible change yet. What ships is a frozen, reviewed design.md — exact env vars, route allow-list, the two new route contracts, the MCP transport/mount shape, and the 18-tool (14 read + 4 write) schema table — that phase 2's four implementer tasks can build against without further architectural decisions.

phases.name: Implement, wire and test the MCP server
phases.ships: A remote Claude client can open a Streamable HTTP connection to the running msfslogger server, authenticate with MCP_TOKEN, list 18 tools, read any part of the logbook (flights, trips, planned legs, ACARS threads, live status, ground session, stats, search), and make the four permitted edits — all without INGEST_TOKEN, the web session, or any existing route's behaviour changing.

phases.title: Ship: wire MCP_TOKEN into the Docker deployment path
phases.ships: A docker-compose-based homelab deployment (this run's target scenario) can actually set MCP_TOKEN and have it reach the container.

tasks.title: Design the MCP auth scope, the two new routes, and the MCP tool/transport contract
tasks.goal: Freeze every architectural decision the four implementation tasks in phase 2 need, so none of them has to guess. Read intake.md in full (.claude/runs/2026-09-18-mcp-server/intake.md) plus the codebase facts it names (docs/api.md, docs/data-model.md, src/auth/ingestScope.ts, src/auth/ingestToken.ts, src/config.ts, src/server.ts, src/auth/middleware.ts) before writing design.md.
acceptance_criteria: design.md has a numbered section per topic below, so implementation tasks can cite it as `ctx.sh design 2026-09-18-mcp-server <n>`.

Auth section: names the exact env var (MCP_TOKEN), states whether it is required-with-fatal-refusal-to-start (like INGEST_TOKEN) or optional-with-MCP-disabled-when-unset, states the minimum-length warning policy, and specifies src/auth/mcpToken.ts + src/auth/mcpScope.ts as new files mirroring src/auth/ingestToken.ts + src/auth/ingestScope.ts's shape exactly (digest-once-at-construction, timingSafeEqual, a hardcoded TS route-allow-list constant — not an env var, matching how INGEST_SCOPED_ROUTES is actually implemented today despite its ALL-CAPS name). States explicitly, with a one-line justification, why this cannot share a digest, a module, or a constant with the ingest token/scope (success criterion 4: revoking one must not affect the other).

Auth section also states how the new gate composes with requireAuth/requireSameOrigin in src/auth/middleware.ts (extend them to recognize an 'mcp' scope result the way they recognize 'ingest' today, or keep the MCP endpoint's own auth fully separate from /api's requireAuth chain) and justifies the choice.

Route-allow-list section: lists every method+path pair MCP_SCOPED_ROUTES must cover to serve all 18 tools (14 read + 4 write), cross-referenced against docs/api.md's existing routes, including the two new ones from the next section.

New-routes section: for GET (path TBD by design, e.g. /api/flights/stats) and GET (path TBD, e.g. /api/flights/search) — exact path (registered before /flights/:id, same reason /flights/combine is), query parameters, response JSON shape, and which src/db/flights.ts functions compute them (aggregate hours/distance/most-flown aircraft & routes; free-text match over notes/airports). States the routing-order constraint explicitly.

MCP transport section: states the exact npm package (e.g. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk) and version constraint, Streamable HTTP session mode (stateless vs. stateful — a homelab single-operator deployment is the deciding fact), the exact mount path(s) in src/server.ts, and how the SDK's request handling coexists with the already-mounted express.json() body parser.

Tool-implementation section: states explicitly whether each tool handler (a) makes an internal HTTP call back into the same server's existing routes (reusing MCP_SCOPED_ROUTES as a real Express-level gate, mirroring the ingest architecture) or (b) calls the underlying src/db/*.ts / route-handler logic in-process (bypassing HTTP entirely, in which case MCP_SCOPED_ROUTES becomes a documentation/audit list rather than a live gate) — and justifies the choice given this server has no existing precedent for (a). Whichever is chosen, states how each tool's error path maps to an MCP tool error (isError content vs. a thrown JSON-RPC error).

Tool inventory table: one row per tool (18 total — 14 read, 4 write) naming its MCP tool name, input schema (fields, types, required/optional), the exact route or function it calls, and the output shape. get_weather's row states explicitly that it calls src/weatherClient.ts's getCachedWeather(icao) directly rather than proxying through POST .../acars-messages/wx, because that route's side effect (writing an ACARS message row) would make a nominally read-only tool mutate the logbook.

update_flight_notes's row states the exact mechanism that keeps `aircraft` unreachable even though PATCH /api/flights/:id accepts it: the tool's own zod input schema has no `aircraft` field and the handler forwards only `{ notes }` to updateFlight(), never req.body verbatim.

create_trip, assign_flight_to_trip and import_simbrief_leg's rows each name the exact existing route they call (POST /api/trips, POST /api/trips/:id/flights, POST /api/planned-legs/simbrief) and confirm no new backend logic is needed for them, per intake.md's frozen decision.
States, in one line, the default taken on the open question in intake.md (TLS + bearer-token secrecy only, no IP allow-list in v1) so it is recorded rather than silently assumed.
Contains no implementation code beyond schema/type stubs and the route table.
`ctx.sh map 2026-09-18-mcp-server` (once design.md exists) correctly lists every section added, confirming the numbering is stable for later citation.
